title: Book Three · Chapter 163: Eighteen on Sunday
story:
Sunday is Ronan's eighteenth birthday.

The spring afternoon is warm. He meets Anna, Kai, and Lin in the park, where Lin has brought two rackets and a shuttlecock.

“A different ball,” Kai says.

Ronan looks at the little white feathers.

“Very little ball.”

Lin shows him how to hold one racket. She sends the shuttlecock across the grass, and he swings too late.

It drops beside his foot.

“No need to run after that one,” Anna says.

“It is being kind.”

He picks it up and tries again. This time, the racket meets it. The white shape goes high and falls behind Lin.

Kai runs to fetch it, then takes Ronan's turn. His quick hands help, but his first return goes straight into the grass.

“Kind again,” Ronan says.

They laugh and change places. Soon Anna and Lin can keep it in the air for several turns.

Ronan watches beside Kai until Mum and Dad arrive with food. Mum has her green and grey bag. Dad carries the water.

They share the warm buns on a bench. Dad asks about the little white ball. Lin gives him a racket and shows him the handle.

Ronan watches him try two slow returns. Mum claps when the second reaches Lin.

“The oldest player,” Kai says softly.

Dad turns. “The best audience, then?”

Kai lifts both hands and laughs.

Dad gives the racket back to Lin. Ronan moves closer to the bench so he can take the water from him.

“Your turn, Mum?” Lin asks.

Mum looks at the rackets, then at the food.

“One try.”

She puts the green and grey bag beside the bench. Lin shows her the handle, just as she showed Ronan.

Mum's first swing reaches the shuttlecock, but it drops very close to her.

Ronan bends to fetch it.

“A family skill,” he says.

“Yours went behind Lin,” Mum answers.

“A larger family skill.”

Dad laughs and holds the cups while Mum gives the racket back. She has not promised another round. She sits down with her own bun and watches the next players.

Ronan takes a drink beside her. He often thinks about costs and dates. For a little while, he is only watching the game.

While Dad and Mum watch Lin play with Kai, Anna gives Ronan a paper bookmark. There is a little roof shape at the top.

“For your books.”

He thanks her and turns it over carefully.

“Better than my shoe drawing.”

“I still have the shoe.”

He slips the bookmark into his jacket pocket. She straightens its top so the small roof does not fold.

He smiles. She touches the blue cord around his wrist, then takes his hand.

For a little while, they watch the shuttlecock move between the rackets. There are different cities on their papers at home. Here, her shoulder is warm beside his.

Mum calls them back for the last buns. Anna holds the cups while Ronan pours water for them both.

Afterward, he takes another turn with the racket. He misses once, then sends a short return toward Lin.

She reaches it and sends it back. This time, he is ready.

The little white shape rises between them. Behind him, he can hear his friends and parents counting the good returns together, and Anna's voice is the clearest of all.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

racket＝球拍；shuttlecock＝羽毛球；feather＝羽毛；bookmark＝书签。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan哪天满十八岁？球拍和羽毛球由谁带来，大家是否一开始就都打得很好？
2. Anna送了什么、还保留着什么旧物？这一生日有没有替两人保证将来同城？

## 读句子

**This time, he is ready.**

拆开看：This time, / he / is ready.

这一次／他／已经准备好接球。
